title: 8-bit batching quality loss hypotheses & scenario matrix
summary: Working worksheet to capture hypotheses about quality vs throughput when moving production serving to 8-bit kernels plus larger batching. Intended to inform regional capacity planning: GPU per-region throughput estimates, SLO risk banding, and fallback routing rules. This is an exploratory sheet (notes + simple model rows) rather than finalized capacity numbers.
background_notes: Motivation: dedicated demand growth in EU and APAC appears to outpace current fp16 fleet expansion. We can trade model precision (8-bit quant) and more aggressive batching to get 1.6-2.4x token throughput on some model families, but we need to capture expected quality degradation per workload and define safe rollout policies. This doc collects measured deltas from small A/B tests, formulates throughput estimates, and proposes guardrails (per-route quality thresholds, automatic rollback triggers).
primary-questions: What is the p50 token latency and tokens/sec improvement for INT8 kernels vs FP16 at batch sizes 1, 4, 8, 16 on A100-like GPUs?
How much downstream quality (measured by log-perplexity delta and user-facing metric proxy) is acceptable before an automatic fallback to FP16?
Regionally, how many additional QPS/TPS can we safely route to 8-bit variants without violating latency SLOs?
assumptions: Baseline GPU: A100 (40GB) with custom INT8 kernels compiled in runtime v0.9.3
Model family: Llama-like 13B and 33B clones used as representative workloads
Baseline (FP16) measured under uniform small-batch synthetic workload (stable perf)
Network egress and tokenization overhead assumed constant across quant variants
KV-cache memory pressure reduced by ~20% under INT8 in our microbenchmarks

interpretation_notes: Rough guidance: for interactive chat routes (SLO p50 < 120ms), INT8 is safe at batch sizes 1 and possibly 4 for 13B depending on KV-cache hit rate. For larger models (33B+) or instruction/QA surfaces, quality deltas at batch >=4 exceed our conservative threshold (2% downstream proxy). Recommend: stage INT8 with batch<=4 behind a canary route, monitor downstream metric and automated rollback when proxy delta > 1.5% for 24h rolling window.
rollback-and-guardrails:
- Canary windows: 8 hours initial, expand to 72 hours if stable
- Auto-fallback triggers: downstream_metric_delta > 1.5% OR delta_logprob > 0.08 AND user-reported error rate increases > 0.1%
- Per-region cap: do not route >30% of production tokens to INT8 variants in first 2 weeks
- Exhaustive smoke tests on top-100 prompt set before region enablement
regional_capacity_impact: Quick regional planner rules: assume conservative 1.6x effective throughput uplift for 13B INT8 @batch4 when estimating shard counts. For EU region with 200M monthly tokens/day peak, compute required GPUs = ceil(peak_tokens_per_day / (24*60*estimated_tokens_per_gpu_per_min)). Use S3 row estimates to size. Add 15% headroom for burst safety.

Do we prefer per-model conservative defaults or per-route conservative defaults?
